newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. concerned by attacks on refugees, staffers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. concerned by attacks on refugees, staffers.

text.p: The Security Council expressed grave concern on Thursday at a recent increase in attacks on refugees and other civilians in conflict areas and the use of force against them.

A statement read at a brief council meeting said it was necessary to bring to justice those who violate international humanitarian law. It also voiced concern over attacks on U.N. personnel and members of humanitarian organisations in violation of international law.

The statement was the result of a lengthy council debate last month, prompted most recently by large-scale killing of refugees in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly known as Zaire, in Rwanda and in other parts of the central African Great Lakes region.
Refugees, U.N. personnel and aid workers have also been targeted in many other conflicts in recent years from Bosnia to Somalia and from Tajikistan to Central America.

"The Security Council reminds all states and others concerned of the need to bring to justice those who violate international humanitarian law," the statement said, recalling efforts to establish an international criminal court.

Alluding to some of the problems that have beset U.N. peacekeeping, it said it was important to ensure "clear, appropriate and realistic mandates to be implemented in an impartial manner, as well as adequate resources for United Nations peacekeeping operations."

Acknowledging concerns that U.N. involvement in refugee situations might impinge on national sovereignty, the council reaffirmed the principles of "full respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of the states concerned."
It encouraged the secretary-general and all states to "look further into practical ways to enhance the United Nations capacity and capability" in crisis prevention.
